actionItems: Investigate timeout issues in 'NML510 - Trial Balance Report' to reduce failure rate.
Analyze flaky behaviour in 'File upload using SPC420' to determine root causes.
Review changes made around the pivot date for potential impacts on report generation.
Compare error patterns between UAT runs before and after the pivot date.
Monitor for any further regressions in high-risk financial tests.
executiveSummary: 29% of runs for 'NML510 - Trial Balance Report' failed after the pivot, up from 20%.
Flaky behaviour observed in 'File upload using SPC420' increased from 0% to 13%.
The 'RSS570 - Crystal Report' showed a significant improvement, dropping from 40% to 0%.
The increase in failure rates may indicate timing issues affecting report generation.
Flaky behaviour in previously stable tests could reflect instability in the testing environment.
These issues may affect the reliability of financial reporting for stakeholders.
Further analysis of the pivot date changes could clarify the observed patterns.
Monitoring high-risk tests is crucial to maintain confidence in financial operations.
